chunks.arabic_text: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ فُرَاتٍ بْنِ أَحْنَفٍ. رَوَى عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ وَأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: Muhammad ibn Furat ibn Ahnaf. He narrated from his father, from Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon them).

chunks.arabic_text: ضَعِيفُ ابْنِ ضَعِيفٍ، لَا يُكْتَبُ حَدِيثُهُ.

translations.en: Weak son of a weak. His ḥadīth are not to be written.

en.summary: This entry highlights the concept of *da'f al-ab* (weak father) in Shia hadith criticism, where Muhammad ibn Furat's reliability is diminished not only by his own weakness but also by that of his father, Ahnaf. This 'weak son of a weak' designation signifies a compounded deficiency in transmission quality, leading al-Ghada'iri to rule that his individual narrations (*al-fard*) are not accepted for legal derivation (*istidlal*) unless corroborated by stronger chains.
en.seo_question: What is the status of Muhammad ibn Furat ibn Ahnaf in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ فُرَاتٍ: Muhammad ibn Furat, the specific narrator being evaluated.
key_terms.ضَعِيفُ ابْنِ ضَعِيفٍ: Weak son of a weak, a technical term indicating the narrator's father was also weak, compounding the weakness.
key_terms.لَا يُكْتَبُ حَدِيثُهُ: His hadith are not to be written, a specific ruling for this level of weakness.
